gloss: the press corps; group of reporters

definitions.gloss: the press corps; the assembled reporters
definitions.explanation: The reporters covering an event or a public figure, treated as a single body. Most often seen in the phrase {記者団|きしゃだん}に{語|かた}る, describing informal remarks made to waiting journalists.

examples.japanese: {首相|しゅしょう}は{記者団|きしゃだん}に{答|こた}えた。
examples.english: The prime minister answered the reporters.

examples.japanese: {官邸|かんてい}の{前|まえ}で{記者団|きしゃだん}が{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: The press corps was waiting in front of the official residence.

examples.japanese: {大臣|だいじん}は{記者団|きしゃだん}に{対|たい}し、「{現時点|げんじてん}では{何|なに}も{決|き}まっていない」と{述|の}べた。
examples.english: The minister told reporters, "Nothing has been decided at this point."

notes:
{記者|きしゃ} (reporter) plus {団|だん} (group, body). Journalistic vocabulary; you will meet it constantly in news reports but rarely in conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {記者団|きしゃだん}に{語|かた}る: to speak to reporters
- {記者団|きしゃだん}に{対|たい}し{述|の}べる: to state to the press corps
- {記者団|きしゃだん}に{囲|かこ}まれる: to be surrounded by reporters
- {記者団|きしゃだん}の{質問|しつもん}に{答|こた}える: to take reporters' questions

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {記者会見|きしゃかいけん}: press conference — a formal arranged event; talking to the {記者団|きしゃだん} is typically impromptu, in a corridor or doorway
- マスコミ: the mass media — the industry as a whole, not the reporters present at one place
